reviews.title: Absurdly good for the price. Budget OLED that checks all the right boxes.
reviews.comment:
First off, let me get this out of the way - This probably isn't the exact same model as the reviews you might have read about the other X27U monitors. Check the exact model number so there are no surprises. This model is substantially cheaper than those for a reason: the panel on it isn't quite as nice as those.
With that said, it's still a phenomenal display. I have it next to a very good 27" IPS display, and it just eats its lunch. You can't even compare the two, it's not a fair fight. You probably hear a lot about how good the blacks are, but something nobody talks about is how that makes colors look. When you have a crimson red on your IPS display, the nature of it introduces a little bit of grey. It looks good, but then you put that same color on this QD-OLED and its amazing the difference. Its an entirely different color that is richer, bolder, and genuine. Everything on the IPS seems so washed out while everything on this QD-OLED just pops off of your screen.
The build quality is what you would expect from a budget OLED. Its plastic, the I/O has just enough ports, and you just have to look at it long enough to mount it. I can't comment on the stand because this went from the box to a monitor arm. The display is glossy but its not a mirrror by any means.
Performance is great. I used a displayport cabled certififed for high bandwidth and I had no uses when I set the refresh rate to 240hz. When I switched the input to HDMI and turned on my PS5, the PS5 showed that everything that you'd expect works. VRR, HDR, it just works out of the box.
The display is a little dim, but I wouldn't call it unusable by any means. I have my brightness pushed to 100 because I like a bright display and it gets bright enough where I am not complaining. Do I wish it was 50 nits brighter like the other models in this lineup? Yes, but even right next to the IPS display that is 300 nits, I don't really think its that massive of a difference. I love a bright display and I know OLED just can't do that. I could have bought another display that is 300 nits, but then I'd wish it was 350. If I got one that was 400 nits, I'd wish it was 450. This display looks good and that's what's important to me.
Overall, I am giving this a perfect score. It has its flaws, but nothing that wasn't there in the listing. It does exactly what it was advertised to do, and also blew out my expectations for in terms of colors, so 5/5.
reviews.author: Len

reviews.title: Premium Gaming Upgrade – Stunning Colors & Flawless G-Sync
reviews.comment:
I’ve been extremely impressed with this monitor. The colors are absolutely amazing—vibrant, rich, and really make everything from games to everyday use look incredible. HDR performance is beautiful and adds a noticeable level of depth and realism that I didn’t have before.
For gaming, this has been a huge step up. G-Sync works flawlessly, delivering super smooth gameplay with no tearing or stuttering. It genuinely elevated my entire setup and experience.
This is by no means a budget monitor—and it shows. The build quality, performance, and overall experience feel very premium.
There’s a feature that occasionally prompts you to refresh the screen, which I’ve seen some people complain about. Personally, it’s not an issue at all. You can simply choose to do it later, and I actually appreciate that it’s there to help protect the longevity of the panel.
Brightness has also been a non-issue for me. Even in a well-lit room, I have no trouble seeing the screen clearly.
Overall, if you’re looking for a high-end gaming monitor that delivers on performance and visuals, this is absolutely worth it.
reviews.author: Lance Sellers

reviews.title: It's a pretty great QD-OLED monitor (for now)
reviews.comment:
Will update this in the future (2-3 years from now).
Honestly amazed how much of a stark difference the QD-OLED panel is compared to my IPS LED displays. I was able to tell a difference immediately when turning the monitor on, as there is no backlight bleed, so I could see a difference with the pixels being self-luminous.
The setup was pretty straightforward, & honestly I love how the ports are facing outwards & not downwards. It really helps for changing around what's plugged in &/or just plugging/unplugging in general.
The color quality is honestly also just, wow! It's so much more saturated, & I believe correct, than my IPS displays, & since there's no backlight-bleed, it helps keep the colors from being washed out which is a huge plus.
For what I have as a setup, the size is perfect, & honestly I do think this on sale is a pretty good deal/value (from what I can tell).
The one slight downside (for how my eyes are), is the resolution. I honestly would probably be better with a 4k monitor, but this montior is genuinely sharper than my 4k IPS display.
Burn-in prevention can be changed around timing wise, so that it's not as intrusive/interruptive, however it's not that intrusive on the screen to begin with.
All the settings for the monitor seem to be pretty customizable, & I do like the ability to change the relative screen size.
Overall I give this 5 stars for the time being, & will update this in due time!
reviews.author: Ian
